key: ‘Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him: When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the candlestick.’
s: After the princes’ dedication gifts, the LORD gives Moses a charge for Aaron; Rashi, on 8:2, reads it as God consoling Aaron, grieved at having no part in that dedication, with the greater task of the lamps, and Ramban, on 8:2, as alluding to the Hanukkah lights of Aaron’s Hasmonean descendants, kept even after the Temple’s destruction.

evidence.words: לְפִי שֶׁכְּשָׁרָאָה אַהֲרֹן חֲנֻכַּת הַנְּשִׂיאִים חָלְשָׁה אָז דַּעְתּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עִמָּהֶם בַּחֲנֻכָּה לֹא הוּא וְלֹא שִׁבְטוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּבָּ"ה חַיֶּיךָ שֶׁלְּךָ גְדוֹלָה מִשֶּׁלָּהֶם, שֶׁאַתָּה מַדְלִיק וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת … ולא נתברר לי, למה ניחמו בהדלקת הנרות … אבל ענין ההגדה הזו, לדרוש רמז מן הפרשה על חנוכה של נרות שהיתה בבית שני על ידי אהרן ובניו, רצוני לומר חשמונאי כהן גדול ובניו … לא רמזו אלא לנרות חנכת חשמונאי, שהיא נוהגת אף לאחר החורבן בגלותנו
evidence.gloss: [Rashi:] Because when Aaron saw the dedication of the princes he was disheartened that neither he nor his tribe was with them in the dedication; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, yours is greater than theirs, for you kindle and dress the lamps. [Ramban:] It is not clear to me why He consoled him with the kindling of the lamps … But the point of this aggadah is to draw an allusion from the passage to the dedication of lights in the Second Temple through Aaron and his sons, that is, the Hasmonean high priest and his sons … they alluded only to the lights of the Hasmonean dedication, which is kept even after the destruction, in our exile.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Numbers 8:2 and at [124,2] match). Plain sense faithful: 7:84 to 7:88 close the princes’ dedication offerings, and 8:1 to 8:2 give Moses a charge for Aaron. Rashi’s first comment on 8:2 carries the consolation reading exactly. Ramban on 8:2 quotes Rashi, questions why the lamps would console Aaron, and takes the aggadah as an allusion drawn from the passage to the Hasmonean Hanukkah lights, kept after the destruction; the two genuinely differ and the sentence names both without resolving. Ramban’s own plain-sense view (the section completes the laws of the lamps) and his dispute with Ibn Ezra are not needed. Two-commentator form within 60 words; entry-check ok.
